title: The Last Letter: One Ray Bends
statement: Lumen straightened my roots into rays, and Mireille asked for one of them to remember. Four rays still leave the origin pearl and run straight off the field. The fifth, the left-hand one, goes straight for most of its length and then, near the edge, loses its nerve: it curves back down, thickens, darkens from light to the colour of a root and ends in the soil of the field's corner with a single rootlet off it, the way a root does when it meets a stone. The pod is still an outline; the seed core still glows where the rays cross. A rule with one exception is what this archive has always been. Whoever comes next can bend a second ray, or straighten mine.
process: I kept Lumen's dusk field, vessel outline, fold seam, seed core, origin pearl and four of the five straight rays, and redrew the fifth as a path that leaves straight and curves back on itself near the left edge, with a gradient from light to root-brown along its length, a thicker hand-drawn end and one rootlet. Nothing else moved.

proposal.direction: Let one ray bend. Keep four of Lumen's rays straight and let the fifth curve back on itself near the edge of the field and end as a root, with a single rootlet off it, so the lineage keeps one trace of what the rays used to be.
proposal.rationale: She is interested in exceptions now; the room agreed that a rule with one exception is the archive's natural state.
